title: A zero-dimensional field-fibre point gives a locally quasi-finite neighbourhood
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Algebraic stacks mean [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], fibred groupoids and $2$-fibre products mean [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], and algebraic spaces mean [def-trf-algebraic-space]. A morphism is representable if every scheme base change is an algebraic space. Properties of representable maps are tested after scheme base change on etale scheme charts. Let $\mathcal X/S$ be an algebraic stack and $h:A\to\mathcal X$ a morphism from an algebraic space locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $a:\operatorname{Spec}k\to\mathcal X$ be a field-valued object [def-weil-field] and $F=A\times_{\mathcal X}\operatorname{Spec}k$, with projection $p:F\to A$. If $z\in|F|$ satisfies $\dim_zF=0$, there is an open subspace $A'\subset A$ containing $p(z)$ for which $h|_{A'}$ is locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite]. Open subspace means an inclusion becoming an open immersion after every scheme base change [def-weil-open-immersion]. Dimension at a point of an algebraic space is computed on an etale scheme chart, using the infimum of dimensions of open neighbourhoods in that chart. No Noetherian or quasi-compactness hypothesis on $A$ or $\mathcal X$ is imposed.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-stack-diagonal-space-source-representability], both $h:A\to\mathcal X$ and $a:\operatorname{Spec}k\to\mathcal X$ are representable: the required diagonal hypothesis is part of [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. Thus $F$ is an algebraic space. By [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus], its map $g:F\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, being the base change of $h$, is locally of finite type.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-source-local-property-locus-descent] to $P=$ locally quasi-finite. Arbitrary base change and fppf target descent are [lem-sfb-representable-lqf-calculus-descent]. Etale source locality reduces on scheme charts to [lem-a1-scheme-lqf-etale-source-locality]: the intersections of two scheme charts are the etale scheme refinements supplied by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], and the forward and converse implications apply to their projections. For a jointly surjective etale family, apply the converse implication to the single surjective etale map from the scheme coproduct of the refined charts [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]; it is etale and locally quasi-finite over the target because both properties are checked on the open summands. For a locally finite type $E\to T$ with $T$ a scheme, take the open $Q_{E/T}$ of [lem-sfb-space-quasifinite-locus-open]. It is the largest open with $P$: the definition of $Q$ tests quasi-finiteness on every scheme chart, and affine witnesses for a point of an open subscheme are witnesses in the ambient scheme [pqf-def-quasifinite]. Its scheme-base-change equality is exactly the last clause of the same locus node. The descent lemma therefore gives a largest open $W_h\subseteq A$ with $h|_{W_h}$ locally quasi-finite, and identifies $p^{-1}(W_h)$ with the largest locally quasi-finite open $W_g$ of $F$.

source.place: Tag 06ME (lemma-quasi-finite-at-point), proof; canonical locus descent: stacks-properties.tex Tags 06M3 and 06M5(2); zero-dimensional chart argument: spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 04NV and morphisms.tex Tag 0397.

proof.text: We show $z\in W_g=Q_{F/k}$, using the scheme-target locus of [lem-sfb-space-quasifinite-locus-open]. Let $c:U\to F$ be any etale scheme chart and $u$ any point above $z$. By the chart definition of dimension in the statement, $\dim_{u_0}U_0=\dim_zF=0$ for some etale scheme chart $c_0:U_0\to F$ and some $u_0\in U_0$ above $z$. This value does not depend on the chart: $u$ and $u_0$ represent the same point $z$, so their field-valued points agree after a common field extension $K$, and the resulting $K$-point of the scheme $U\times_FU_0$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] lies over a point $w$ mapping to $u$ and to $u_0$. Both projections of $U\times_FU_0$ are etale, being base changes of the etale charts, so [lem-sfb-etale-topological-dimension-at-point] gives $\dim_uU=\dim_w(U\times_FU_0)=\dim_{u_0}U_0=0$. The minimum description in [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point] gives an open neighbourhood $V\subseteq U$ of $u$ with $\dim V=0$. For every $v\in V$, $0\leq\dim_v V\leq\dim V=0$. The fibre of $V\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ at its unique target point is $V$ itself, and this map is locally of finite type by the chartwise hypothesis and restriction. Consequently [lem-trf-locally-quasi-finite-relative-dimension-zero] shows $V\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally quasi-finite. The affine witness at $u$ in $V$ is also an affine neighbourhood in $U$, so $U\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is quasi-finite at $u$ by [pqf-def-quasifinite]. Since the chart and lift were arbitrary, the definition of $Q_{F/k}$ gives $z\in Q_{F/k}$.

proof.text: The equality $W_g=p^{-1}(W_h)$ and $z\in W_g$ imply $p(z)\in W_h$. Set $A'=W_h$. This is an open subspace containing $p(z)$, and the construction in Step 2 gives precisely that $h|_{A'}$ is locally quasi-finite.
